tokyo-okutama-and-chichibu-mountain-loop.title: Tokyo · Okutama and Chichibu Mountain Loop
tokyo-okutama-and-chichibu-mountain-loop.slogan: A 188 km loop out of Hachioji
tokyo-okutama-and-chichibu-mountain-loop.story: Close to Tokyo, but the road language is mountains, not blocks. A 188 km loop that starts and ends near Hachiōji, about 3 h 14 of riding. On the way it passes Okutama lake road, Chichibu forest bend core and Nagatoro river stop. The highest point is about 800 m.

scenicChapters.title: Col de l Iseran → Col du Galibier
scenicChapters.narrative: Height already gained and held. The road stays near 2764 m for 141 km instead of surrendering it to the next valley. Exposed ground: wind matters more here than gradient. Nothing blocks it.

scenicChapters.title: Col de Montgenevre
scenicChapters.narrative: Cold comes early up here and stays late. Ride it with something in reserve: the summit is not the end of the work, only the middle of it. The last of the trees go and the road runs out onto open ground. The summit sits at 2642 m, and what surrounds it is rock, weather and distance.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

scenicChapters.title: Col d Izoard → Col de Vars
scenicChapters.narrative: 68 km that neither climbs nor drops much. The road settles into the ground rather than fighting it — this is where a day makes up time without anyone trying. Third and fourth, and very little else.

route-des-grandes-alpes-col-de-l-iseran-.story: A one-way ride of 290 km, Val-d'Isère to Embrun - roughly 4 h 04 in the saddle. The stops in between: Col du Galibier and Col d Izoard. The highest point is 2,764 m. Col du Galibier, Col d Izoard and Col de Vars are subject to seasonal closure - check it is open before you set off. A steady touring day rather than a sprint.

waypoints.name: San Bernardino pass road
waypoints.advice: You top out at 2066 m here. The road climbs 1473 m on the way up to it, steadily. Reckon on about 10 °C colder than the valley, and more in the wind. Nothing on this route is higher. At this height the road is a summer one: snow gates can stay shut into June and shut again in October. Next is Mesocco, mostly downhill.

waypoints.advice: The route ends here after 184 km. You lose 1276 m on the way down to it, steadily.

sections.advice: Chur fuel and status gate → San Bernardino pass road climbs about 1473 m in 60 km. This is the part worth slowing down for - look through the bends and use the pull-offs.
San Bernardino pass road → Mesocco food reset drops about 1276 m over 16 km. Brakes and eyes forward; the views are behind the corners, not in them.

scenicChapters.title: Ticino Lakes and Valleys Route
scenicChapters.narrative: Slow enough to look. The surface follows the shoreline, so the corners arrive where the water decided, not where an engineer did. Water arrives beside the road and stays for 18 km. The line follows the shore because there is nowhere else for it to go.
